New Technologies.title: How I write software with LLMs - Hacker News Discussion

New Technologies.title: Andrej Karpathy on Jevons Paradox and AI-Generated Software
New Technologies.description: Andrej Karpathy shared thoughts on how 'working software increasingly comes out on a tap' and Jevons paradox kicks in - demand for software grows substantially. He mentions you can 'ask for anything - explainers, visualizers, dashboards, bespoke single-use apps' and '10X your test suite, auto-optimize code, run giant research projects'. Says 'Free your mind' (Matrix reference).
New Technologies.author: Andrej Karpathy (quoted by Simon Willison)

New Technologies.title: Datasette Agent Edit Plugin
New Technologies.description: Simon released datasette-agent-edit 0.1a0, a base plugin for agentic text editing. Implements view, str_replace, and insert tools inspired by Claude text editor design. This enables plugins for collaborative Markdown editing, updating SQL queries, and editing SVG files.
New Technologies.author: Simon Willison

New Technologies.title: Running Python Code in a Sandbox with MicroPython and WASM
New Technologies.description: Simon released micropython-wasm 0.1a2, his latest sandboxing experiment that bundles a WASM build of MicroPython with wasmtime wrapper. He's using it for a code execution sandbox plugin for Datasette Agent called datasette-agent-micropython. Notes that GPT-5.5 has so far failed to break out of the sandbox.
New Technologies.author: Simon Willison

New Technologies.title: Claude Fable 5: Mid-tier Results on Coding Tasks
New Technologies.description: Hacker News discussion comparing Claude Fable 5's performance on coding tasks. Key insights: Claude is described as 'a much better planner' while 'Codex is a much more professional coder.' Discussion notes you can 'mask a surprisingly amount of terrible coding with proper planning' and explores trade-offs between different AI coding assistants.
New Technologies.author: Hacker News Community

New Technologies.title: Claude Fable is Relentlessly Proactive - HN Discussion
New Technologies.description: Hacker News discussion on Simon Willison's observation about Claude Fable 5 being 'relentlessly proactive'. Critics noted that Claude models 'write too much unnecessary code, burn excessive tokens, and create unnecessary tests.' Community discussion about the trade-offs of aggressive AI assistance in development workflows.
New Technologies.author: Hacker News Community

New Technologies.title: Fable Refuses to do LLM-related Work
New Technologies.description: Hacker News discussion reporting that Claude Fable 5 refuses to help with developing LLMs or answering questions about LLM-related topics. This relates to Anthropic's invisible safeguards policy for frontier LLM development that was later walked back after community outrage.
New Technologies.author: Hacker News Community

New Technologies.title: What it Feels Like to Work with Mythos
New Technologies.description: Hacker News discussion about working with Claude Mythos 5. Key insight: AI creates 'inefficient code, but doing it at lightspeed with minimal effort,' resulting in unmaintainable code. Discussion explores the trade-offs between speed and maintainability when using AI coding assistants.
New Technologies.author: Hacker News Community

New Technologies.title: State of AI in 2026: LLMs, Coding, Scaling Laws, China, Agents, GPUs, AGI
New Technologies.description: Lex Fridman Podcast episode #490 featuring Nathan Lambert and Sebastian Raschka discussing the comprehensive state of AI in 2026. Topics include LLMs and coding, scaling laws, AI agents, GPU developments, AGI progress, China's role in AI, programming and developer tooling, and open vs closed LLMs.
New Technologies.author: Lex Fridman with Nathan Lambert and Sebastian Raschka

New Technologies.name: Claude Fable 5
New Technologies.description: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 model launched with enhanced coding capabilities, topping the SWE-bench Verified benchmark at 95.0%. Available via Claude API, AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry with stronger coding, knowledge work, vision, memory, and long-context performance.
community_quotes: Tops the SWE-bench Verified benchmark at 95.0%
Safer general-use model with stronger coding abilities
One of the best AI models for coding as of June 2026

New Technologies.title: Gemini CLI Shutdown Announcement
New Technologies.description: Google announced the shutdown of Gemini CLI for free, Pro, and Ultra users on June 18, 2026. Google is transitioning users to the new Antigravity CLI. Both Gemini CLI and Gemini Code Assist IDE extensions will stop serving Google AI requests on June 18, 2026.

community_feedback.quote: It's not an IDE, it's a way to run agents. I expect Gemini CLI getting axed for...
Users reporting performance problems: One user called Gemini CLI 'UNUSABLE' after experiencing 1 minute 4 seconds of processing time
Gemini CLI will stop working from June 18, 2026

Others.title: AI enthusiasts are in a race against time, AI skeptics are in a race against entropy
Others.description: Charity Majors captures the dynamic between AI enthusiasts and skeptics: Enthusiasts are seeing discontinuous leaps in capabilities and can't afford to wait, while skeptics are seeing reliability degrade and institutional knowledge evaporate when code ships faster than engineers can read it. The key insight: there is no natural feedback loop connecting these two groups.
Others.author: Simon Willison (quoting Charity Majors)

Others.name: zero.xyz
Others.description: Platform that gives AI agents instant access to over 8,000-9,000 tools, APIs and services without requiring individual API keys or account configurations, unblocking agents to discover and use services autonomously.
community_quotes: Like OpenRouter for agent tools
Unblocks your agents so they can discover services autonomously

Others.name: Powabase
Others.description: Backend-as-a-service platform for AI-native applications combining PostgreSQL, RAG, AI agents, memory management, workflows, and automation primitives in a single PostgreSQL-native stack, solving the complexity of building AI apps with tightly coupled vector storage.
community_quotes: Solves the complexity of building AI apps with RAG and agents by providing a PostgreSQL-native stack
Tightly couples vector storage with traditional database functionality
#1 Product on May 27, 2026

Others.name: Phasr
Others.description: Open-source productivity tool that enables running 100+ workflows simultaneously without losing context, designed for AI-powered task management and workflow orchestration.
community_quotes: Run 100+ workflows simultaneously without losing context

Others.name: Calling Skills for AI Agents
Others.description: Developer tool that enables AI agents and coding assistants to add voice and video calling capabilities via GitHub integration, expanding the communication modalities available to AI development tools.
community_quotes: Add voice and video calling via your coding agent

Others.title: AI Enthusiasts vs. Skeptics: Race Against Time vs. Entropy
Others.description: Charity Majors captures the dynamic between AI enthusiasts and skeptics: enthusiasts race against time as teams that don't adopt AI could face existential threats from competitors, while skeptics race against entropy as shipping code faster than engineers can read degrades reliability and institutional knowledge. The key issue is there's no natural feedback loop connecting the two groups.
Others.author: Simon Willison (citing Charity Majors)

Others.title: Revisiting Using AI Coding Assistants: You're Holding It Wrong Edition
Others.description: Developer-focused discussion examining proper usage patterns for AI coding assistants and common mistakes developers make when integrating AI tools into their workflows. Highlights best practices and anti-patterns in AI-assisted development.
Others.author: Hackaday

Others.name: Qursor
Others.description: Point at any UI to send exact context to your AI. An inspector tool that captures precise UI elements and sends accurate context to AI assistants, solving issues with command misalignment and token waste in AI interactions.
community_quotes: Launch of the Day on June 12, 2026
#3 Product of the Day
Solves command misalignment in AI coding
Reduces token waste in AI interactions

Others.title: AI Enthusiasts vs Skeptics: Race Against Time vs Entropy
Others.description: Simon highlighted Charity Majors' analysis of the dynamic between AI enthusiasts and skeptics in software teams. Enthusiasts see 'discontinuous leaps in capabilities' and teams that sit this out 'could be out of business before the dust settles'. Skeptics note that when you 'ship code faster than engineers can read it', you make withdrawals from trust accounts, reliability degrades, and systems become incomprehensible. Charity notes 'There is no natural feedback loop connecting enthusiasts with skeptics' and designing feedback loops to 'mend the gap in shared reality' is a key organizational design problem.
Others.author: Simon Willison (quoting Charity Majors)
